questions.question: What was the approximate monetary loss alleged by the State Bank of India (SBI) in its complaint against Anil Ambani and his company Reliance Communications Ltd, that triggered the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI) investigation in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹3,000 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** initiated a high-profile investigation in **August 2025** following a formal complaint lodged by the **State Bank of India (SBI)**.
 
• The complaint alleged a significant **monetary loss** to the tune of approximately **₹3,000 crore** involving credit facilities extended to the telecom major. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The primary entities named in the investigation are **Anil Ambani** and his flagship telecom firm, **Reliance Communications Ltd (RCom)**.
 
• The probe was triggered after internal audits and forensic reports suggested potential irregularities in the utilization of funds sanctioned by the **State Bank of India** and other consortium members.
 
• The investigation focuses on alleged **diversion of funds**, **criminal conspiracy**, and **cheating**, which resulted in the account being classified as a non-performing asset and subsequently a fraudulent account.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reliance Communications (RCom):**
 
 
• Once a dominant force in the Indian **telecommunications** industry, **Reliance Communications** faced a massive debt crisis due to intense competition and high spectrum costs.
 
• The company officially entered the **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC)** process in **2019** to resolve its mounting liabilities, which exceeded **₹46,000 crore** at that time.
 
 
 
• **Role of the CBI in Bank Frauds:**
 
 
• The **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)** is the premier investigating agency of **India** that handles cases of **corruption** and **economic offenses** of national and international importance.
 
• Its **Banking Fraud Evolution Cell** specifically targets high-value **bank defaults** and **white-collar crimes** that threaten the financial stability of **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)**.
 
 
 
• **State Bank of India (SBI):**
 
 
• As the **largest public sector bank** in **India**, **SBI** often acts as the **lead bank** in large corporate loan consortiums.
 
• Under **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** guidelines, banks are mandated to report accounts as **fraud** to the **CBI** if they find evidence of **willful default** or **misappropriation** of sanctioned loans.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework for Financial Crimes:**
 
 
• Cases involving large-scale banking fraud are typically registered under **Section 420** (Cheating) and **Section 120-B** (Criminal Conspiracy) of the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)**, often alongside provisions of the **Prevention of Corruption Act**.
 
• The **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** may also join such probes to investigate **money laundering** aspects under the **PMLA (Prevention of Money Laundering Act)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timeline:** The specific complaint and subsequent action by the **CBI** in this context were recorded in **August 2025**.
 
• **Impact:** Investigations into figures like **Anil Ambani** highlight the rigorous scrutiny of **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)** in the Indian banking system, which have historically weighed down the **economy**.
 
• **Numerical Value:** The figure of **₹3,000 crore** represents the approximate principal loss alleged by **SBI** in this specific instance of the investigation.

questions.question: Which of the following best characterises the India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR) framework?

options.text: A cultural-exchange mechanism involving arts and heritage institutions only
A forum exclusively for defence procurement negotiations
A high-level mechanism to deepen bilateral cooperation across strategic, economic, technological, and people-to-people sectors
A platform limited to trade dispute settlement between the two countries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A high-level mechanism to deepen bilateral cooperation across strategic, economic, technological, and people-to-people sectors**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR)** is a distinctive high-level leadership mechanism designed to pave a new path for the **Strategic Partnership** between the two nations.
 
• The **inaugural meeting** of the ISMR was held in **September 2022** in **New Delhi**, marking a significant shift toward a more integrated and future-oriented bilateral engagement.
 
• It brings together senior ministers from both countries, including the Ministers of **External Affairs**, **Finance**, and **Commerce**, to deliberate on cross-cutting issues that affect **strategic, economic, and technological** domains.
 
• The primary objective of the ISMR is to identify and capitalize on new opportunities in emerging sectors, ensuring that the **bilateral relationship** evolves in line with global shifts in **technology** and **sustainability**.
 
• During the **second ISMR** held in **Singapore** in **August 2024**, both countries reaffirmed their commitment to deepening cooperation and decided to elevate the relationship to a **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Six Pillars of Cooperation:** The ISMR framework is structured around six key pillars: **Digitalization**, **Skill Development**, **Sustainability**, **Healthcare**, **Advanced Manufacturing**, and **Connectivity**.
 
• **Economic Significance:** **Singapore** has consistently been one of the largest sources of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** into India, and the ISMR helps streamline **trade** and **investment** flows by resolving regulatory bottlenecks.
 
• **Digital Connectivity:** A major achievement discussed within this framework is the **real-time payment systems linkage** between India’s **UPI** and Singapore’s **PayNow**, which was launched in **February 2023** to facilitate faster and cheaper cross-border remittances.
 
• **Green Energy and Sustainability:** Both nations are collaborating closely on **Green Hydrogen** and **Green Ammonia** initiatives to meet their respective **Net Zero** targets, emphasizing the **sustainability** pillar of the roundtable.
 
• **Semiconductor Ecosystem:** In the **2024** meeting, a specific emphasis was placed on building a resilient **semiconductor supply chain**, with Singapore offering its expertise in **advanced manufacturing** to support India's **Semicon India** mission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leadership Participation:** The **2nd ISMR** saw participation from Indian ministers **Dr. S. Jaishankar** (External Affairs), **Nirmala Sitharaman** (Finance), **Piyush Goyal** (Commerce and Industry), and **Ashwini Vaishnaw** (Electronics and IT).
 
• **Strategic Alignment:** The framework aligns with India’s **Act East Policy**, positioning **Singapore** as a crucial gateway for India’s engagement with the **ASEAN** region.
 
• **Human Capital:** The **Skill Development** pillar focuses on the **mutual recognition of qualifications** and the **skilling** of the Indian workforce to meet the demands of Singapore’s **high-tech industries**.
 
• **IMEC Corridor:** Discussions often include broader regional connectivity, such as the **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)**, where **Singapore** can play a role as a global logistics hub.

questions.question: A 24-hour wildlife census using the waterhole method, which recorded the sighting of 73 Great Indian Bustards, was conducted in June 2025 in which of the following national parks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Desert National Park**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **24-hour wildlife census** using the **waterhole method** was conducted in **June 2025** at the **Desert National Park (DNP)**, which spans across the **Jaisalmer** and **Barmer** districts of **Rajasthan**.
 
• During this census, a significant sighting of **73 Great Indian Bustards (GIBs)** was recorded, providing vital data for the conservation of this **Critically Endangered** species.
 
• The **waterhole method** is a traditional counting technique where volunteers and forest officials stay stationed at specific water points for a full day and night, usually during the **peak summer** months when animals are most likely to visit water sources.
 
• The **Desert National Park** is the primary natural habitat and the last stronghold for the **Great Indian Bustard** in the world, making such surveys crucial for monitoring their population trends.
 
• The census in **2025** aimed to assess the impact of ongoing conservation efforts, including the **predator-proof fencing** and **captive breeding programs** established in the region. ***Hence, the correct answer is Desert National Park.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Desert National Park (DNP):**
 
 
• Located in the **Thar Desert**, it covers an area of approximately **3162 sq km**, making it one of the largest national parks in India.
 
• It was declared a National Park in **1981** to protect the fragile ecosystem of the desert and its unique wildlife like the **Chinkara**, **Desert Fox**, and **Blackbuck**.
 
• The park features a unique landscape of **sand dunes**, jagged rocks, and dense salt lake bottoms, providing a perfect camouflage for the **Great Indian Bustard**.
 
 
 
• **Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps):**
 
 
• It is the **State Bird of Rajasthan**, locally known as **Godawan**.
 
• The bird is listed under **Schedule I** of the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, granting it the highest level of legal protection in India.
 
• On the **IUCN Red List**, it is categorized as **Critically Endangered** due to its small, declining population, primarily threatened by **overhead power lines**, **habitat loss**, and **stray dogs**.
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** launched **Project Great Indian Bustard** to facilitate the recovery of the species through **in-situ** and **ex-situ** conservation.
 
 
 
• **Other Options in Context:**
 
 
• **Ranthambore National Park:** Situated in **Sawai Madhopur**, Rajasthan, it is famous for its **Royal Bengal Tiger** population rather than bustards.
 
• **Bandhavgarh National Park:** Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, it is known for having one of the highest densities of tigers in India.
 
• **Kanha National Park:** Also in **Madhya Pradesh**, it is renowned for the **Barasingha** (Swamp Deer) and its role in tiger conservation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Waterhole Census Technique:** This method relies on the physiological need of animals to drink water during extreme heat. In **Rajasthan**, this is often conducted on **Buddha Purnima** (full moon night) to ensure maximum visibility for observers sitting in "machans" near the waterholes.
 
• **Conservation Milestones:** A successful **conservation breeding center** has been established at **Sam, Jaisalmer**, where GIB eggs are collected from the wild, hatched in incubators, and the chicks are reared to bolster the wild population.
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The **Great Indian Bustard** is a **flagship species** for the grassland ecosystem. Its presence indicates the health of the dry grasslands, which are often overlooked compared to forested ecosystems.
</ul

questions.question: Which Ministry is responsible for the grant increase in national championships for high-priority sports?

options.text: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS)** is the primary government body responsible for formulating and implementing policies related to sports and youth development in **India**.
 
• In **2023**, the ministry announced a significant revision in the financial assistance provided under the **Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs)**.
 
• Under the revised guidelines, the grant for organizing **National Championships** for **High-Priority** sports disciplines was increased from **₹22 lakh** to **₹44 lakh**. ***Hence, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is the correct answer.***
 
• This increase applies to **Senior, Junior, and Sub-Junior** categories, aiming to improve the quality of competition, infrastructure, and technical conduct of the tournaments.
 
• The **High-Priority** category includes sports where **India** has high medal-winning potential in international events like the **Olympics**, **Asian Games**, and **Commonwealth Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs):**
 
 
• This is the flagship scheme of the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** through which funds are channeled for training, international exposure, and equipment.
 
• It supports the **National Coaching Camps**, appointment of **Foreign Coaches**, and participation in **International Competitions**.
 
• The categorization of sports into **High Priority**, **Priority**, and **General** determines the level of financial support provided.
 
 
 
• **Categorization of Sports:**
 
 
• **High Priority:** Disciplines like **Athletics**, **Archery**, **Badminton**, **Boxing**, **Shooting**, and **Wrestling**.
 
• **Priority:** Sports that are included in the **Olympic Games** but where **India** is currently working towards global standards.
 
• **General:** Sports that are not included in the **Olympics** or **Asian Games** but have a significant following or regional importance.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives of the Ministry:**
 
 
• **Khelo India Programme:** Launched in **2018** to revive the sports culture in **India** at the grassroots level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the country.
 
• **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS):** A specialized program to provide personalized support to **India’s** elite athletes to improve their performance at the **Olympic Games**.
 
• **National Sports Development Fund (NSDF):** Established in **1998** to mobilize resources from non-government sources for the promotion of sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports:** It was initially set up as the **Department of Sports** just before the **9th Asian Games** in **1982** in **New Delhi**. It became a full-fledged **Ministry** in the year **2000**.
 
• **Role of SAI:** The **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**, an autonomous body under the **Ministry**, manages the field-level implementation of various schemes and maintains sports infrastructure like the **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** and **Indira Gandhi Arena**.
 
• **National Sports Policy:** The current framework is guided by the **National Sports Policy 2001**, which focuses on "**Broadening of Sports**" and "**Achieving Excellence in Sports**" at the national and international levels.
 
• **Financial Budget:** For the financial year **2024-25**, the budget allocation for the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** was increased to over **₹3,400 crore**, reflecting the government's commitment to the "**Viksit Bharat**" vision through sports.

questions.question: The Supreme Court declared in October 2025 that the principle of public trust extends to artificial lakes this ruling affirmed the directive of which of the following High Court benches?

options.text: Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court
Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court
Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court
Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Supreme Court of India**, in a landmark judgment delivered in **October 2025**, expanded the legal horizon of environmental protection by ruling that the **Public Trust Doctrine** applies equally to **artificial lakes** and man-made water bodies.
 
• This specific ruling affirmed a previous directive issued by the **Nagpur Bench** of the **Bombay High Court**, which had emphasized that the state acts as a trustee for all water resources regardless of their origin. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court.***
 
• The court observed that the ecological significance of a water body does not depend on whether it was formed naturally or constructed by human intervention, as both serve vital **environmental functions** like groundwater recharge and climate regulation.
 
• The **Public Trust Doctrine** mandates that the state holds certain resources in trust for the general public and cannot permit their conversion for private ownership or commercial exploitation that harms the public interest.
 
• This judgment reinforces the interpretation of **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**, which encompasses the right to a wholesome environment as part of the **Right to Life**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Public Trust Doctrine:** 
 
 
• Originating from **Roman Law**, it was first integrated into Indian law by the **Supreme Court** in the case of **M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997)**.
 
• It establishes that resources like **air, sea, waters, and forests** have such a great importance to the people as a whole that it would be wholly unjustified to make them a subject of private ownership.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Framework:** 
 
 
• **Article 48A**: This **Directive Principle of State Policy** directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
 
• **Article 51A(g)**: It is a **Fundamental Duty** of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment, including **lakes**, rivers, and wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Bombay High Court:** 
 
 
• Established on **August 14, 1862**, it is one of the oldest and most prestigious High Courts in India.
 
• It has jurisdiction over the states of **Maharashtra** and **Goa**, and the Union Territory of **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**.
 
• The **Nagpur Bench** is one of its permanent benches, along with **Aurangabad** and **Panaji**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Artificial Lakes:** 
 
 
• In many urban areas, **artificial lakes** are the primary sources of **micro-climate maintenance** and biodiversity hubs.
 
• Protecting them under the Public Trust Doctrine prevents land mafias and developers from reclaiming lake beds for **real estate** projects.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The ruling is expected to impact various **smart city projects** and urban development plans across **India** where man-made reservoirs were previously considered exempt from strict environmental non-alienation rules.
 
• The **October 2025** verdict clarifies that once a territory is designated as a water body in **revenue records**, its status cannot be changed easily, even if it is currently dry or was originally man-made.
 
• This legal precedent provides a powerful tool for **environmental activists** to challenge the encroachment of historic tanks and reservoirs constructed during various eras of Indian history.
</ul

questions.question: By how many basis points did the Reserve Bank of India reduce the repo rate in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 basis points**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **April 2025** monetary policy review, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** announced a reduction in the **Repo Rate** by **25 basis points** (bps) to stimulate economic activity.
 
• The decision was finalized by the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** after evaluating the prevailing **inflation** trends and the need to support **GDP growth** in the new financial year.
 
• A reduction of **25 basis points** translates to a **0.25%** decrease in the interest rate at which the **RBI** lends to commercial banks. ***Hence, the correct answer is 25 basis points.***
 
• The **MPC** opted for a calibrated **25 bps** cut rather than a more aggressive **50 basis points** or **75 basis points** reduction to ensure that **liquidity** remains balanced without stoking **consumer price index (CPI)** inflation. ***Hence, options 1 and 4 are incorrect.***
 
• Small adjustments like **10 basis points** are generally not standard practice for the **RBI**, which typically moves in multiples of **25** to provide a clear signal to the **financial markets**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Repo Rate:** 
 
 
• The **Repo Rate** (Repurchase Option) is the **key policy rate** used by the **Central Bank** to control the **money supply** and **inflation** in the economy.
 
• When the **Repo Rate** is reduced, it becomes cheaper for **commercial banks** to borrow from the **RBI**, which usually leads to lower **interest rates** for **home loans**, **auto loans**, and **business credits**.
 
 
 
• **Basis Points (bps):** 
 
 
• In **finance**, a **basis point** is a unit equal to **one-hundredth of one percent** (**0.01%**).
 
• It is primarily used to denote changes in **interest rates**, **equity indices**, and the **yield** of a fixed-income security to avoid ambiguity in percentage discussions.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):** 
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** committee constituted by the **Central Government** under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• It is headed by the **Governor of the RBI** and meets at least **four times a year** to determine the **policy interest rate** required to achieve the **inflation target**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on the Economy:** A **25 basis point** cut in **April 2025** signals a "dovish" stance, indicating that the **RBI** is prioritizing **economic expansion** over strict **monetary tightening**.
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:** While the **Repo Rate** is the rate at which banks borrow, the **Reverse Repo Rate** is the rate at which the **RBI** borrows money from banks. The gap between these two rates is known as the **corridor**.
 
• **Transmission of Rates:** For a **repo rate** cut to benefit the public, **commercial banks** must transmit the benefit by lowering their **MCLR (Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate)** or **External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR)**.
 
• **Inflation Targeting:** The primary mandate of the **RBI** is to maintain **price stability**, with a target **inflation** rate of **4%** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%** (i.e., between **2%** and **6%**).
</ul

Exclusive pension scheme for all transgender persons

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inheritance rights and access to education and employment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of Tamil Nadu** released the **Tamil Nadu Transgender Policy 2025** to provide a comprehensive legal framework for the rights and welfare of transgender persons.
 
• A landmark provision of this policy is the explicit assurance of **inheritance rights**, allowing transgender individuals to inherit ancestral and parental property, addressing a long-standing legal gap. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The policy emphasizes **inclusive education** by ensuring **non-discriminatory access** to schools and colleges, alongside creating specialized **employment** opportunities in both public and private sectors.
 
• It streamlines the process for obtaining **Transgender Identity Certificates** and **Identity Cards**, facilitating easier access to various government welfare schemes and **legal documentation**.
 
• The policy was developed following directives and observations from the **Madras High Court** to ensure the **dignity** and **social integration** of the community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:** **Tamil Nadu** has been a pioneer in transgender welfare, being the **first state** in India to establish a **Transgender Welfare Board** in the year **2008**.
 
• **Nodal Agency:** The **Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department** is responsible for the implementation and monitoring of the **2025 Policy** guidelines across the state.
 
• **Healthcare Provisions:** The state provides **Gender Reassignment Surgery (GRS)** free of cost in **Government General Hospitals** and includes transgender persons under the **Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme**.
 
• **Housing and Social Security:** While the state provides **free housing site pattas** and a **monthly pension** of **₹1,500** for destitute transgender persons over the **age of 40**, the **2025 policy** specifically strengthens the legal standing regarding **property inheritance**.
 
• **Education Incentives:** The government provides **tuition fee waivers** and **scholarships** for transgender students pursuing higher education to improve the **literacy rate** and **economic independence** within the community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Rights:** The policy aligns with the **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019**, but goes further by addressing **succession laws** which are usually governed by personal laws.
 
• **Reservation Status:** In **Tamil Nadu**, transgender persons are currently categorized under the **Most Backward Classes (MBC)** for the purpose of **reservation** in education and **government jobs**.
 
• **Sensitization:** The **2025 policy** mandates **sensitization programs** for **police personnel**, **healthcare workers**, and **judicial officers** to prevent **harassment** and **stigma**.
 
• **Self-Identification:** It upholds the right to **self-identified gender**, in accordance with the **Supreme Court's NALSA judgement (2014)**, ensuring that individuals do not face medical coercion for legal recognition.

questions.question: Lala Lajpat Rai, whose 160th birth anniversary was observed on 28 January 2025, was popularly known by which title?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab Kesari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai** was a prominent Indian independence activist and a revolutionary leader, widely celebrated by the title **Punjab Kesari**, which means the **'Lion of Punjab'**.
 
• He was born on **28 January 1865** in the village of **Dhudike**, located in the **Ferozepur district** of **Punjab**. His **160th birth anniversary** was observed across India on **28 January 2025**.
 
• He was a vital part of the **Indian National Congress** and formed the legendary **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio, representing the assertive nationalist wing alongside **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** and **Bipin Chandra Pal**.
 
• In **1894**, he was instrumental in founding the **Punjab National Bank (PNB)**, which was the first **swadeshi bank** started with Indian capital. He also founded the **Lakshmi Insurance Company**.
 
• During a protest against the **Simon Commission** in **Lahore** on **30 October 1928**, he was severely injured in a **lathi charge** ordered by the British police. He succumbed to his injuries on **17 November 1928**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Netaji:**
 
 
• This title is synonymous with **Subhash Chandra Bose**, one of the most influential leaders of the Indian independence movement who led the **Indian National Army (INA)**.
 
• The title **Netaji** was reportedly first used by Indian soldiers of the **Indische Legion** in **Germany** in **1942**.
 
 
 
• **Lokmanya Tilak:**
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was conferred with the title **Lokmanya**, which means **"accepted by the people"**.
 
• He was a scholar, mathematician, and philosopher who famously declared, **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!"**
 
 
 
• **Deshbandhu:**
 
 
• **Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das)** was popularly known as **Deshbandhu**, which translates to **"Friend of the Nation"**.
 
• He was a distinguished lawyer, a leader of the **Swaraj Party**, and a political mentor to **Subhash Chandra Bose**.
 
 
 
• **Literary Contributions of Lala Lajpat Rai:**
 
 
• He was a prolific writer and authored several influential books, including **Unhappy India**, **Young India**, **History of My Deportation**, and **The Arya Samaj**.
 
• He founded the **Servants of the People Society** in **1921**, dedicated to the service of the country and its marginalized communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Political Ideology:** **Lala Lajpat Rai** was deeply influenced by the **Arya Samaj** and played a significant role in the **Swadeshi Movement** of **1905** following the **Partition of Bengal**.
 
• **International Impact:** He traveled to the **United States** in **1917** and founded the **Indian Home Rule League of America** in **New York** to seek international support for India's freedom.
 
• **Education:** He was a pillar of the **DAV (Dayanand Anglo-Vedic) College Trust and Management Society** and helped establish several educational institutions in **Punjab**.
 
• **Legacy:** His death sparked a wave of revolutionary activities; **Bhagat Singh**, **Rajguru**, and **Sukhdev** vowed to avenge his death, which eventually led to the **Saunders' murder case** in **1928**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the 2025 Guinness World Record recently set by Nigerian chess master Tunde Onakoya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longest chess marathon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tunde Onakoya**, a renowned **Nigerian chess master** and child education advocate, officially broke the **Guinness World Record** for the **longest chess marathon** in **April 2024**.
 
• The record-breaking event took place at the iconic **Times Square** in **New York City**, beginning on **April 17** and concluding on **April 20, 2024**.
 
• Onakoya played for a continuous duration of **60 hours**, significantly surpassing the previous record of **56 hours, 9 minutes, and 37 seconds**, which was set by Norwegian players **Hallvard Haug Flatebø** and **Sjur Ferkingstad** in **2018**.
 
• The marathon was not just a feat of endurance but a **fundraising campaign** aimed at raising **$1 million** for his non-profit organization, **Chess in Slums Africa**, to support education and chess training for underprivileged children across the continent.
 
• Throughout the attempt, he was joined by American chess player **Shawn Martinez**, who acted as his opponent for the entire **60-hour** duration to satisfy the **Guinness World Record** requirements. ***Hence, the correct answer is Longest chess marathon.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chess in Slums Africa:**
 
 
• This is a social intervention initiative founded by **Tunde Onakoya** in **2018**.
 
• The organization uses **chess** as a framework to help children in **impoverished communities** (like **Oshodi** in **Lagos, Nigeria**) develop **critical thinking**, **problem-solving skills**, and access to **scholarships**.
 
• The foundation has successfully reached thousands of children, providing them with a path away from **street life** and **child labor**.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• The event drew global attention, receiving public support from **Bill Gates**, the **President of Nigeria** (**Bola Ahmed Tinubu**), and various **United Nations** representatives.
 
• Onakoya’s achievement has been hailed as a **symbol of resilience** and a testament to the potential of **African youth** on the global stage.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Rules of the Record:**
 
 
• According to **Guinness World Record** guidelines for the **longest marathon**, the participant is permitted only **5 minutes** of break for every **hour** of continuous activity.
 
• These breaks can be accumulated, which **Tunde Onakoya** used for brief periods of **rest** and **medical check-ups** during his **60-hour** stint.
 
• Despite battling **physical exhaustion** and **intense fatigue**, he remained **undefeated** in the games played during the marathon.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Legacy:**
 
 
• By the end of the marathon, the campaign had successfully raised **hundreds of thousands of dollars**, contributing significantly toward the construction of **educational facilities** in **Nigeria**.
 
• The record solidified the **year 2024** as a milestone for **Nigerian sports** and **humanitarian efforts** globally.

questions.question: Which of the following was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development during the National Consultation on Gender Budgeting in June 2025?

options.text: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Annual Report 2024
One-Stop Centre scheme for women affected by violence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gender Budgeting Knowledge Hub portal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gender Budgeting Knowledge Hub (GBKH) portal** was launched by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)** to act as a centralized **digital repository** for all resources related to **Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB)** in India.
 
• It was officially unveiled during the **National Consultation on Gender Budgeting** held in **June 2025** (referring to the event timeline specified), aimed at strengthening the **institutionalization** of gender-sensitive planning across **Government departments**.
 
• The portal serves as a platform for sharing **best practices**, **training modules**, **research papers**, and **Gender Budgeting Statements** from various **Union Ministries** and **State Governments**. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Gender Budgeting Knowledge Hub portal.***
 
• The primary objective of this hub is to facilitate **capacity building** for officials and stakeholders, ensuring that **financial allocations** effectively address the specific needs and **disparities** faced by women and girls.
 
• By providing **real-time access** to data and guidelines, the **GBKH portal** streamlines the process of monitoring **gender-related expenditures** and evaluating the impact of **welfare schemes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gender Budgeting in India:**
 
 
• India formally adopted **Gender Budgeting** in **2005-06**. It is not a separate budget for women but an analytical tool to ensure **gender mainstreaming** in the **macroeconomic policy** framework.
 
• The **Ministry of Women and Child Development** serves as the **nodal agency** for coordinating these efforts across the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):**
 
 
• Launched in **January 2015** at **Panipat, Haryana**, this scheme aims to address the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote **female education** and **empowerment**.
 
• While an **Annual Report** might be released periodically, it was not the specific portal launched during the **June 2025** consultation focused on budgeting.
 
 
 
• **One-Stop Centre (OSC) Scheme:**
 
 
• Also known as **Sakhi Centres**, this scheme was implemented to provide **integrated support** (medical, legal, and psychological) to **women affected by violence** under one roof.
 
• It is funded through the **Nirbhaya Fund** and is a critical component of the **Sambal** sub-scheme of **Mission Shakti**.
 
 
 
• **National Resource Centre for Women (NRCW):**
 
 
• This was an initiative intended to provide **technical support** to the **Ministry** and other agencies; however, the specific **Knowledge Hub portal** is the contemporary digital evolution designed for **Gender Budgeting** specifically.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mission Shakti:** This is an **integrated women empowerment programme** launched as an umbrella scheme for the **safety, security, and empowerment** of women. It has two sub-schemes: **'Sambal'** (safety) and **'Samarthya'** (empowerment).
 
• **Gender Budgeting Statement (Statement 20):** This is a crucial document presented along with the **Union Budget** in **Parliament**, highlighting the **quantum of funds** allocated for schemes that benefit women.
 
• **Article 15(3)** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers the State to make **special provisions** for women and children, providing the legal foundation for **Gender Budgeting**.
 
• The **June 2025** consultation focused on the **sustainable development goals (SDG 5)**, which targets **gender equality** and the empowerment of all women and girls by **2030**.
</ul

questions.question: Who received the Padma Vibhushan in 2025 for their contributions to the dance form, Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumudhini Lakhia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumudhini Lakhia**, a legendary **Kathak** dancer and choreographer, was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan** in the year **2025** for her exceptional contribution to the field of **Art**.
 
• Born in **1930**, she is widely credited with revolutionizing the traditional **Kathak** dance form by moving away from solo narratives toward innovative **group choreographies** and contemporary themes.
 
• She founded the **Kadamb Centre for Dance** in **Ahmedabad**, **Gujarat**, in **1964**, which has since become a premier institute for training and research in **Kathak**.
 
• Her work is characterized by a focus on **spatial design**, lighting, and costumes, which transformed the visual aesthetics of the dance while maintaining the integrity of the **Lucknow Gharana** techniques.
 
• Before receiving the **Padma Vibhushan**, she was previously decorated with the **Padma Shri** in **1987** and the **Padma Bhushan** in **2010**, making her one of the most decorated classical dancers in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Padma Vibhushan:** 
 
 
• It is the **second-highest civilian award** in **India**, preceded by the **Bharat Ratna**.
 
• The award was instituted on **January 2, 1954**, and is given for "exceptional and distinguished service" without distinction of race, occupation, position, or sex.
 
• The awards are announced annually on the eve of **Republic Day** (**January 26**) by the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
 
 
• **Kathak Dance Form:** 
 
 
• **Kathak** is one of the **eight classical dances** of **India** recognized by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi**.
 
• It originated in **North India**, specifically in the states of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**.
 
• The name is derived from the Sanskrit word **'Katha'**, meaning story, and practitioners are known as **Kathakars** (storytellers).
 
• Key features include **Chakkars** (spins), intricate **footwork** (Tatkar), and expressive gestures (Abhinaya).
 
 
 
• **Other Distinguished Personalities:** 
 
 
• **Birju Maharaj:** A doyen of the **Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin Gharana** of **Kathak**. He received the **Padma Vibhushan** in **1986** and passed away in **2022**.
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra:** A legendary exponent of **Odissi** dance. He was the first person from **Odisha** to receive the **Padma Vibhushan** in the year **2000**.
 
• **Shobana Chandrakumar:** A renowned **Bharatanatyam** dancer and two-time **National Film Award** winning actress from **Kerala**. She was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **2006**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Padma Awards** are conferred by the **President of India** at ceremonial functions held at **Rashtrapati Bhawan** usually around **March** or **April**.
 
• In **2025**, the selection committee emphasized pioneers who bridged the gap between **traditional heritage** and **modern sensibilities**, fitting the profile of **Kumudhini Lakhia** perfectly.
 
• She has been a mentor to several prominent dancers, including **Aditi Mangaldas** and **Daksha Sheth**, who have further expanded the boundaries of **Indian classical dance**.
 
• The recognition of a **Kathak** exponent with the **Padma Vibhushan** highlights the continued cultural significance of the **Gharana system** in the **21st century**.
</ul

questions.question: What key capability of the Vertically-Launched Short-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VLSRSAM) was established during its March 2025 flight-test?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Near-boundary low-altitude engagement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **March 14, 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and the **Indian Navy** successfully conducted a flight test of the **Vertically Launched Short Range Surface to Air Missile (VLSRSAM)**.
 
• The test was carried out from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur**, located off the coast of **Odisha**, using a land-based vertical launcher.
 
• The primary objective of the mission was to establish and validate the **near-boundary low-altitude engagement** capability of the missile system, which is crucial for defending against **sea-skimming** threats.
 
• The missile successfully intercepted a **high-speed aerial target** flying at a very **low altitude** and at a **near-range boundary**, demonstrating the system's precision and rapid reaction time.
 
• This flight test confirmed the integration of various subsystems, including the **missile**, the **vertical launcher** with **canister**, and the **weapon control system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **VLSRSAM System Overview:**
 
 
• The **VLSRSAM** is a next-generation, ship-borne weapon system designed to provide a **point-defense** shield for **Indian Navy** warships against a variety of aerial threats.
 
• It is intended to replace the older **Barak-1** surface-to-air missile systems currently in service on several Indian naval vessels.
 
• The missile has an operational range of approximately **40 to 50 kilometers** and can reach altitudes of up to **15 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Design and Technology:**
 
 
• It features **cruciform wings** that provide aerodynamic stability and **Thrust Vector Control (TVC)**, allowing the missile to perform high-maneuverability turns immediately after a vertical launch.
 
• The **vertical launch** capability ensures a **360-degree** coverage, enabling the ship to engage targets coming from any direction without maneuvering the vessel or the launcher.
 
• The system is equipped with an **active radar seeker** for terminal guidance, ensuring high kill probability against agile targets.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance:**
 
 
• The development of **VLSRSAM** is a significant step toward **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) in the defense sector, as it is designed and developed indigenously by **DRDO** laboratories like **RCI Hyderabad** and **DRDL**.
 
• It is specifically optimized to counter **supersonic sea-skimming missiles**, which fly very close to the water surface to avoid radar detection, making **low-altitude engagement** a critical requirement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with other options:**
 
 
• **Underwater deployment:** This capability is associated with **Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missiles (SLBMs)** or torpedoes, not the **VLSRSAM**, which is surface-launched.
 
• **Mid-course ballistic target destruction:** This is the domain of **Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD)** systems like the **Prithvi Air Defence (PAD)** or **Advanced Air Defence (AAD)**, rather than short-range tactical missiles.
 
• **Long-range high-altitude interception:** Systems like the **S-400** or **Long Range Surface-to-Air Missile (LRSAM/Barak-8)** handle long-range threats, whereas **VLSRSAM** is specialized for **short-range** protection.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Prof. Syed Wajih Ahmad Naqvi, an outstanding Biogeochemical Oceanographer with national and international recognition, received the 2024 Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar in which of the following categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vigyan Shri (VS) Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prof. Syed Wajih Ahmad Naqvi**, a distinguished **Biogeochemical Oceanographer**, was honored with the **Vigyan Shri (VS) Award** in **2024**.
 
• He received this prestigious recognition in the domain of **Earth Science** for his pioneering contributions to marine science and biogeochemistry. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP)** is the highest national award in the field of science, technology, and innovation in **India**, established to recognize outstanding contributions by scientists and technologists.
 
• The **Vigyan Shri (VS) Award** specifically recognizes **distinguished contributions** to any field of science and technology.
 
• Prof. Naqvi has significantly enhanced the understanding of **oceanic nitrogen cycles**, particularly in the **Arabian Sea** and the **Indian Ocean**, gaining both national and international acclaim.
 
• He previously served as the **Director** of the **CSIR-National Institute of Oceanography (NIO)**, based in **Goa**, where he led numerous research expeditions and institutional developments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (RVP) Categories**:
 
 
• **Vigyan Ratna (VR)**: Awarded for **lifetime achievements** and contributions in any field of science and technology.
 
• **Vigyan Shri (VS)**: Awarded for **distinguished contributions** in any field of science and technology.
 
• **Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar (VY-SSB)**: Designed to recognize young scientists up to the **age of 45 years** who have made exceptional contributions.
 
• **Vigyan Team (VT)**: Awarded to a **team** consisting of **three or more** scientists/researchers for collaborative work.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility and Domains**:
 
 
• The awards are given in **13 specific domains**, including **Physics, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, Mathematics & Computer Science, Earth Science, Medicine, Engineering Sciences, Agricultural Science, Environmental Science, Technology & Innovation, Atomic Energy, Space Science and Technology**, and **Others**.
 
• The selection is made by the **Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar Committee (RVPC)**, which is headed by the **Principal Scientific Adviser** to the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 2024**:
 
 
• The year **2024** marked the **inaugural edition** of the Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar, consolidating various previous science awards under one umbrella.
 
• A total of **33 awards** were announced in the first edition across the four categories.
